tb21_profile.skill: Launch a QEMU guest headless in the background with its serial console redirected onto a TCP socket (-serial telnet:127.0.0.1:6665,server), get the guest to actually reach a getty login prompt on that console, and block until the port answers before returning while leaving the VM running
tb21_profile.domain: QEMU system emulation, -serial / console redirection over TCP, telnet, Alpine boot to getty on ttyS0, backgrounded long-running processes
tb21_profile.task_form: configure-a-service / environment bring-up: start a detached process, expose a network endpoint, poll for readiness, leave it up

verifier_notes: CORRECTION PASS (fix-team 04, promote_pass.py). Two CalibForge tasks that the original pass held out under the FREE rule are now in final_top10; I read both test suites myself before promoting. (1) system-administration_20260601_053159_008 (bridge agetty onto TCP 7777/7778, one auto-login root, one password-gated, log the sessions, auto-restart after a kill, survive concurrent clients) was FREE only in the frozen packet; work/verifier_strength.json now grades it `ok` and that is if anything generous. Its ten tests are almost all live-socket behaviour: they connect() to each port, drive a real login, send `echo <timestamped marker>` and `whoami` and require the marker and `root` to come back over the socket, then `pkill -9 socat` / `fuser -k` each port and require it to answer again within 4s. Only the two log-file checks are exists/non-empty. Promoted to rank 3. (2) system-administration_20260615_143301_008 is STILL graded FREE in work/verifier_strength.json and I am overriding that deliberately; the automated check will flag it. The grade is a heuristic false negative, and I confirmed the earlier team's report by reading tests/test_outputs.py. It has two tests. test_telnet_login_prompt pipes through `socat - TCP4:127.0.0.1:6666` and asserts 'login:' appears in what comes back -- the heuristic scored that as a substring check without noticing the haystack is network output from a socket that must be listening and must be serving a getty. test_telnet_login_success writes an expect(1) script that spawns `telnet 127.0.0.1 6666`, expects 'login:', sends consoleuser, expects 'Password:', sends consolepass, expects a shell prompt, then sends `echo LOGIN_SUCCESS` and requires LOGIN_SUCCESS to echo back before printing LOGIN_VERIFIED, which the assertion looks for; every branch has an explicit timeout that exits 1. Nothing short of a real listener with a working PAM login and a live shell passes that -- no file-exists or file-content path exists at all, since the task writes no files. Promoted to rank 2. Displaced: system-administration_20260507_172207_002 (a service-start-ordering race; it touches only the 'block until ready' clause and nothing of the console-on-a-port crux) and system-administration_20260606_153537_008 (background a server and socat its socket onto TCP -- the same mechanism 053159_008 now covers, plus the getty/login layer this task actually needs). Unchanged from the original pass: task_001082_5357146e and task_009677_2b79022d are `strong` in the strength file but were never ranked in per_source, so they are not eligible; tw_10263 / tw_332536 / tw_101115 / tw_186081 are FREE in both sources and stay out.

notes: Read the verifier_notes before using this file. The two best teachers for qemu-startup are both excluded by the FREE rule: system-administration_20260615_143301_008 is a near-verbatim restatement of this task ('telnet-accessible login prompt on port 6666, background, leave it running') and I checked its tests - they open a real TCP connection, expect a login prompt, log in with expect and require a live shell, so the FREE grade is a heuristic false negative on the word 'substring'. system-administration_20260601_053159_008 (serial console servers over TCP with automatic root login) is FREE only in the packet, `ok` in the current strength file. If the merge step trusts the newer work/verifier_strength.json rather than the packet snapshot, it should reinstate 053159_008 immediately, and it should consider whether 143301_008 is worth a manual override - it is the highest-value single item I found for this task. CalibForge is again the corpus that changes the answer: it has the only task that actually boots a guest in QEMU end to end, plus a well-verified cluster on backgrounded daemons, start-ordering races and socket-to-TCP bridging. TMax's 24-task QEMU cluster is broader than I expected here - several entries genuinely daemonize a VM, redirect -serial, and probe its port - so it holds four of the final ten. Terminal-Lego contributes the QEMU flag-syntax task and solid readiness/TCP-plumbing material. Recursive-Task-Synthesis is usable for once: its GRUB/ttyS0 serial-console cluster is real domain overlap and rts_task_307df6c5ff13c7eccf218e2a is a clean block-until-ready task, though all of it is `absent`. SWE-Smith and SWE-Rebench have nothing that starts a VM or blocks on a port; their ranks 5-10 are honest filler. Note for the merge: the packet grades and work/verifier_strength.json disagree for about a quarter of all shown candidates pool-wide, so the FREE check must pick one source and apply it uniformly; I applied FREE-if-either.
